blocks.title: Monte Irvin Orange Park
blocks.html: One of the original Olmsted-designed landscapes in the Essex County Park System, Monte Irvin Orange Park spans nearly 48 acres in the heart of the city. Named for baseball Hall of Famer and Orange native Monte Irvin, it features athletic fields, a man-made lake, walking paths, a basketball court, a synthetic-grass soccer field, and a community center that opened in late 2025.

blocks.title: Star Tavern
blocks.html: A City of Orange institution since 1945, Star Tavern has built its reputation on one thing: consistently exceptional thin-crust bar-style pizza. The New York Times has called it superior, loyalists have been making the trip for generations, and the no-frills atmosphere, humming with nearly 80 years of neighborhood character, is as much a draw as the pie itself.

blocks.title: Thomas Edison National Historical Park
blocks.html: Just minutes away in West Orange, Thomas Edison National Historical Park preserves the laboratory and home where America's most prolific inventor changed the world. Visitors can tour Edison's working laboratory complex and Glenmont, his Victorian estate, for an immersive look at where the phonograph, motion picture camera, and countless other innovations were born.

blocks.title: Orange House Cafe
blocks.html: Located at the Orange Train Station on Lincoln Avenue, Orange House Cafe is a European-style cafe and bakery serving coffee, tea, fresh pastries, and a thoughtfully assembled menu of sandwiches and light fare. It's the kind of neighborhood spot that makes a commute or a slow morning genuinely worth looking forward to.

blocks.title: Sunsplash Caribbean Bakery & Juice Bar
blocks.html: A family-owned City of Orange staple for over 25 years, Sunsplash specializes in authentic Caribbean and vegetarian cuisine, along with a standout juice bar. From jerk chicken and curry goat to Jamaican beef patties, coco bread, and signature sea moss and wheatgrass drinks, the menu is a genuine taste of the Caribbean right on Main Street.

items.q: What's the purchase limit for a single cannabis delivery order?
items.a_html:
New Jersey law allows you to buy up to the equivalent of 28.35 grams, or one ounce, of usable cannabis per transaction. That can include any combination of the following:

  • Dried Flower/Bud: 28.35 grams (1 ounce).
  • Concentrates/Resin/Oils: 4 grams (solid or liquid/vaporized oil).
  • Ingestible Items (Gummies/Edibles): 1,000 mg of THC (roughly ten 100mg packages).
  • Maximum Possession Limit: Up to 6 ounces of cannabis and cannabis products.
  • Mixing Products: You can mix and match, for example, by purchasing 1/2 ounce of flower and 2 grams of concentrates.
  • Daily Limits: The 1-ounce limit is generally considered a daily limit across all dispensaries.

items.q: What taxes will I pay on a cannabis delivery order in New Jersey?
items.a_html: New Jersey adult-use cannabis purchases include a 6.625% state sales tax, a 2% municipal transfer or user tax, where applicable, and a $2.50-per-ounce Social Equity Excise Fee (SEEF). All of these apply to delivery orders exactly as they do to in-store purchases, and every applicable charge is itemized at checkout before you confirm.
